source_family_policy.scope: Source-derived article prose, connected interpretation, title/dek, notes, caption/alt and any new substantive brief language. Identical portable article is one authored text, not a second derivation. Mirrors and page/PDF versions of the same district passage form one family.
source_family_policy.quotations: No quoted verse or song. At most25 verbatim nonsong words/source; at most10 song words. Internal full-page images are inspection evidence, not public reprints.
source_family_policy.proposed_headroom: Keep Dash narrative and note below150 before shared metadata. Other families have ample room for a short article. Photo descriptions and credit belong to Commons family, not Dash.

sources.title: Socio-cultural and Literary Potential of the Traditional Odia Oral Narratives: A Critical Review
sources.author: Pratap Kumar Dash
sources.publisher: SSRG International Journal of Humanities and Social Science / Seventh Sense Research Group
sources.type: Authored literary review, not a named-performer interview or transcribed recording
sources.access: Original PDF downloaded; title/date and section text extracted. Full printed40 image personally viewed. Initial network-restricted curlDNS resolved through authorized network retrieval.
supported_claims: Dash describes a strolling singer invoking Jagannath and Ganesh and calls the songs Lokahitabani.
His thematic examples include family unity, opposition to dowry abuse, conduct, Gandhi and the three monkeys.
limits: Attribute examples to Dash rather than a universal programme or every performer.
Omit unsupported cake-name etymology and universal visiting calendar.
No named singer, locality, fieldwork date or full song transcription is supplied in section3.1.
Do not turn the author's moral summary into an endorsement of all views he lists.
sources.rights: PDF states CC BY-NC-ND4.0. No article figure reused; internal page evidence only. Public original paraphrase with citation, no lyrics quoted.
